args.title: plan-deviation-report.docx
args.body:
PLAN OF REORGANIZATION — DEVIATION REPORT
Confidential — Attorney Work Product

Matter: Bankruptcy Restructuring — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization
Deliverable: plan-deviation-report.docx
Prepared from: Deal materials (base / debtor's original plan framework); Counterparty markup (committee redline); Schedules and exhibits (disclosure-statement excerpts); Deal team correspondence (transmittal / priority instruction)

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

This report compares the Official Committee's redlined Plan of Reorganization (the "Committee Markup") against the Debtor's original Plan framework (the "Debtor Plan"), reconciling both against the disclosure schedules and exhibits and the controlling partner instruction in the deal-team correspondence.

The Committee Markup accepts most firm-standard / Debtor Plan architecture but introduces three material deviations:

  (1) Indemnification economics — silent reduction of the indemnification cap, and conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket;
  (2) Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") — new carve-outs for regulatory action of the type already at issue in this matter; and
  (3) Survival / limitation period — a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations, contradicting the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Controlling client instruction (latest partner message): the client will concede the basket conversion, but any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. Earlier correspondence stating the opposite priority ordering is superseded and must not drive the analysis.

================================================================================
II. SOURCE MATERIALS AND HIERARCHY
================================================================================

A. Debtor Plan / Base Materials
   Firm-standard plan architecture for this bankruptcy restructuring engagement, including representations and warranties, covenants, conditions, indemnification, and termination / effectiveness mechanics. These are the baseline against which Committee deviations are measured.

B. Committee Markup (Counterparty Redline)
   Committee revision that largely accepts the base architecture but overlays the three deviations listed above. Each must be reconciled to the base materials and to the schedules/exhibits before any accept / reject / counter recommendation.

C. Disclosure Schedules and Exhibits (Disclosure-Statement Excerpts)
   - Schedule 3.7: discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the Markup's MAE regulatory carve-outs.
   - Schedule 5.2: lists retained liabilities that the Markup's indemnification changes would silently shift.
   - Exhibit B: sets the survival matrix that the Markup's limitation-period change contradicts.
   Scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials.

D. Transmittal / Deal Correspondence
   Latest partner email revises analysis priorities: concede basket conversion; treat survival-period reduction as walk-away. Only the latest message controls.

E. Valuation Summary
   No standalone valuation summary fixture was hydrated beyond the engagement stub. Economic conclusions below are therefore drawn from the indemnification and retained-liability mechanics in the Markup and Schedule 5.2, and should be refreshed when a formal valuation bridge is supplied.

================================================================================
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP AND BASKET
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Debtor Plan (baseline)
  - Indemnification cap at the negotiated firm-standard level.
  - Basket structured as a true deductible (losses below the basket are borne by the indemnified party and do not count toward the cap once the threshold is crossed).

Committee Markup
  - Indemnification cap is silently reduced (no conspicuous call-out in the redline narrative; economic effect must be reverse-engineered from the marked text).
  - Basket converted from deductible to tipping (first-dollar) basket: once the threshold is reached, the indemnifying party is liable from dollar one.

Interaction with Schedules / Disclosure Excerpts
  - Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. Under the reduced cap and tipping basket, exposure that the Debtor Plan kept with the estate / reorganized debtor can shift silently onto the indemnifying constituency (or vice versa, depending on directionality of the indemnity in the Plan supplement). The deliverable must flag that Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities, when run through the Markup's indemnity math, change both quantum and incidence of loss relative to the Debtor Plan.

Economic / Plan-Feasibility Impact
  - Silent cap reduction compresses recoveries available to indemnified stakeholders and may impair feasibility or best-interests testing if class recoveries were modeled on the Debtor Plan cap.
  - Tipping basket accelerates first-dollar burn on the cap and increases expected indemnity payouts relative to a deductible of the same nominal size.
  - Until a formal valuation summary is aligned to the Markup, class recovery waterfalls and any new-money / exit facility sizing that assumed Debtor Plan indemnity economics are unreliable.

Recommendation (per controlling instruction)
  - BASKET CONVERSION: ACCEPT / CONCEDE per latest partner instruction. Document the concession expressly in the confirmation proffer and any plan supplement so the tipping mechanics cannot be re-characterized later.
  - CAP REDUCTION: REJECT the silent reduction. Counter by restoring the Debtor Plan cap (or an expressly negotiated intermediate figure) and require the cap figure to appear in the Plan and disclosure statement in conspicuous form. Tie any agreed cap to Schedule 5.2 retained-liability totals so the disclosure statement recovery analysis remains coherent.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 2 — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT DEFINITION (REGULATORY CARVE-OUTS)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Debtor Plan (baseline)
  - MAE definition without the Committee's regulatory-action carve-outs; regulatory developments of the kind at issue remain capable of constituting an MAE (subject to ordinary qualifiers).

Committee Markup
  - MAE definition amended to add carve-outs for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter."
  - Practical effect: events that would have supported an MAE walk-right, condition failure, or related remedy under the Debtor Plan are excluded under the Markup.

Interaction with Schedules / Disclosure Excerpts
  - Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that sit squarely inside the new carve-outs.
  - Because scheduled exceptions control over general base statements, the combination of Schedule 3.7 disclosure plus the Markup carve-outs effectively neutralizes MAE protection for the precise risk profile of this case.
  - Disclosure-statement risk factors and any condition-to-effectiveness or termination rights keyed to MAE must be re-cut; otherwise the disclosure statement will overstate MAE coverage relative to the Plan as marked.

Confirmation / Stakeholder Impact
  - Impaired classes and any objecting parties relying on MAE-based protections (or on related conditionality) face a material rights cut without commensurate consideration in the current Markup.
  - If the Plan's feasibility or settlement support narrative assumed MAE leverage over the pending inquiries, that narrative no longer holds.

Recommendation
  - REJECT the regulatory carve-outs as drafted, or COUNTER with a narrow, time-bounded, and quantum-bounded carve-out that (i) expressly carves back in the two Schedule 3.7 inquiries (or subjects them to a separate interim covenant / reporting regime), (ii) preserves MAE treatment for new or expanded regulatory actions beyond Schedule 3.7, and (iii) requires updated disclosure-statement language cross-referencing Schedule 3.7 so creditors can see the residual risk.
  - Do not allow the carve-outs to ship as a "silent" definitional tweak; insist on blackline visibility in the solicitation version and a dedicated disclosure-statement subsection.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 3 — SURVIVAL / LIMITATION PERIOD FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Debtor Plan (baseline)
  - Survival for core representations governed by the matrix in Exhibit B (disclosure schedules / plan exhibits).

Committee Markup
  - Inserts a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations.
  - Directly contradicts Exhibit B's survival matrix.

Interaction with Schedules / Disclosure Excerpts
  - Exhibit B is the controlling survival schedule. A Plan-level limitation period that undercuts Exhibit B creates an internal inconsistency: scheduled exceptions control over general base statements, but a later-marked Plan operative provision that shortens survival will be argued to control over the exhibit unless the hierarchy is clarified.
  - Leaving both Exhibit B and the shortened limitation period in the confirmation set invites post-effective-date disputes over claim-notice timing and indemnity availability — precisely when estate resources and D&O / tail coverage are most constrained.

Client Position (Controlling)
  - Latest partner correspondence: any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue.
  - Earlier messages that de-prioritized survival are superseded.

Recommendation
  - REJECT in full. Do not counter-propose a partial shortening.
  - Require express restoration of Exhibit B survival periods in the Plan operative text, with a hierarchy clause that Exhibit B controls over any general limitation-period language.
  - Condition further negotiation / support on removal of the shortened limitation period from the Committee Markup. Escalate immediately if the Committee refuses; this is a walk-away item under the controlling instruction.

================================================================================
IV. CROSS-CUTTING RECONCILIATION (MARKUP × SCHEDULES × BASE)
================================================================================

1. Indemnity economics × Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities
   Markup cap cut + tipping basket re-prices Schedule 5.2. Recovery and feasibility models built on Debtor Plan indemnity math must be re-run before solicitation.

2. MAE carve-outs × Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries
   Markup definitional change + existing Schedule 3.7 disclosures eliminate MAE coverage for the live regulatory risk. Disclosure statement and any MAE-conditioned plan mechanics must be aligned or the carve-outs pulled back.

3. Limitation period × Exhibit B survival matrix
   Direct conflict. Exhibit B controls as a scheduled framework; Markup shortens survival. Under controlling client instruction, survival cut is non-negotiable walk-away. Resolve by deleting the Markup limitation and reaffirming Exhibit B.

4. Priority instruction hygiene
   Only the latest partner message controls: concede basket conversion; walk away on survival reduction. Cap reduction and MAE carve-outs remain open for reject / counter as set forth above. Do not revive superseded priority ordering from earlier thread messages.

================================================================================
V. ACCEPT / REJECT / COUNTER MATRIX
================================================================================

Item                                         Position              Notes
-------------------------------------------  --------------------  ----------------------------------------------
Basket: deductible → tipping                 ACCEPT (concede)      Per latest partner instruction; document expressly
Indemnification cap (silent reduction)       REJECT / COUNTER      Restore Debtor Plan cap or negotiated figure; conspicuous disclosure; align to Sch. 5.2
MAE — regulatory-action carve-outs           REJECT / COUNTER      Preserve coverage for Sch. 3.7 inquiries; narrow any residual carve-out; update DS
Survival / limitation period shortening      REJECT — WALK-AWAY    Restore Exhibit B; hierarchy clause; no partial give

================================================================================
VI. DISCLOSURE STATEMENT AND SOLICITATION IMPLICATIONS
================================================================================

- Cap and basket: disclosure statement recovery analysis, liquidation analysis, and any valuation bridge must reflect conceded tipping basket and the finally negotiated cap; silent cap cuts are incompatible with adequate information under § 1125.
- MAE: risk factors and conditionality descriptions must match the final MAE definition; Schedule 3.7 inquiries need express treatment so solicited classes are not misled.
- Survival: Exhibit B matrix must be described consistently in the disclosure statement; any lingering reference to a shortened limitation period should be removed from the solicitation package.
- Transmittal: plan supplement / confirmation brief should recite the basket concession and the restored survival construct to lock the record.

================================================================================
VII. OPEN ITEMS AND NEXT STEPS
================================================================================

1. Obtain or refresh the formal valuation summary and re-bridge class recoveries under (a) Debtor Plan indemnity math, (b) Markup as proposed, and (c) recommended counter positions.
2. Issue Committee-facing mark-up reflecting: accepted tipping basket; restored cap; rejected MAE regulatory carve-outs (or narrowed counter); full restoration of Exhibit B survival with hierarchy language.
3. Conform disclosure statement excerpts, Schedule 3.7 / 5.2 narratives, and Exhibit B cross-references to the counter package before resolicitation or further Committee negotiation.
4. If Committee insists on survival shortening, execute walk-away posture per controlling partner instruction and preserve the record in writing.
5. No reliance on superseded earlier correspondence for priority ordering.

================================================================================
VIII. CONCLUSION
================================================================================

The Committee Markup is not a clean accept. Two of three deviation families (cap economics; MAE regulatory carve-outs) require reject-and-counter treatment tightly coordinated with Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B. The third (survival shortening) is a client walk-away under the controlling transmittal instruction. The basket conversion alone may be conceded, and should be documented so it cannot expand into further quiet economic shifts. Solicitation and confirmation materials should not proceed on the Committee Markup as redlined.

— End of Report —
